Hi Samir / Priya 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a few concrete next steps so we can size Dedicated capacity and schedule the technical deep-dive:

1) Integration + auth
- SDK: we recommend using the Redwood JS/Go SDK for production workloads (examples in the Drive link below).
- Auth: for hosted demos API keys are fine; for Dedicated/Private you can choose customer-managed mTLS or KMS-backed token auth.

2) Routing & model variants
- We support policy routing by latency/cost/region and automated fallback to compatible model variants when a pool is constrained.

3) Structured output / tool calling
- Function-calling (structured output) is supported; we can demonstrate example schemas and validation in the deep-dive.

4) Embeddings & rerankers
- If you're using embeddings for semantic retrieval, we suggest dense embeddings (1536 dim for our default models) + a lightweight reranker for pass-through quality. We can size a separate embedding pool if you want isolation.

5) Dedicated autoscaling & sizing questions we need from you (please fill the attached template):
- Expected sustained QPS and expected peak QPS (requests/sec)
- Average prompt size (input tokens) and average generations (output tokens)
- Desired p50/p95/p99 latency SLOs and tail tolerance during bursts
- Concurrency per-request characteristics (are you doing many short requests or fewer long streaming requests?)

Next steps
- I'll attach a sizing template please fill it with the numbers above and any sample traces you can share.
- Schedule: can we do a 60-min technical deep-dive next Wed or Thu? Aditya (SE) and Dev (infra) will join to walk through SDK, auth, routing, and queueing behavior.

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. A few quick answers while we pull numbers into your template: 

- Sustained QPS: ~12 r/s for our inference endpoint (semantic search + chat mix). Peak bursts up to ~150 r/s for short windows (~30s).
- Average prompt tokens: 220 in, average generation 120 out.
- Latency target: p95 < 300ms for short-answer queries; for long-form generation p95 < 800ms.
- Concurrency: most requests are short (no streaming), but we have background batch reranks that run multiple calls in parallel per user request (so effective concurrency spikes).

1) For burst behavior — can Dedicated support burst capacity beyond the reserved pool? You mentioned a burst buffer in the call. How is that priced/allocated?

Hi Samir — thanks for the numbers, that's super helpful. A few technical notes ahead of the deep-dive: 

SDK/Auth
- SDK: the JS/Go SDKs wrap the REST API and manage retries, streaming, and backoff. We'll share a runbook with init examples (API key, OAuth token flows) and a Private/Dedicated mTLS guide.
- mTLS: supported on Dedicated/Private. For mTLS we exchange client certs via your PKI; we can also do mutual TLS+token combo for rotation.

Routing/Fallbacks
- Policy routing can route by model family (latency vs cost), region, or a customer tag. Fallbacks: we maintain compatibility matrix to fall back to a lower-cost variant when capacity constraints occur.

Structured output / tool calling
- Function-calling is available; the SDK surfaces a typed response and structured validation hooks. This adds minimal latency if you do single-shot calls; for multi-tool orchestration we typically recommend an orchestration tier that handles retries and deterministic routing.

Embeddings & Rerankers
- Embedding recommendation: use our 1536-dim dense embeddings for the initial run. If you want higher recall we can add a cross-encoder reranker as a thin pass (reranker calls are cheap if run only on top-K). We can show cost vs quality tradeoffs in the deep-dive.

Autoscaling / Throughput / Queues
- Baseline pool sizing: as a rule of thumb, estimate tokens/sec = (QPS * avg_input_tokens + QPS * avg_output_tokens). Map tokens/sec to GPU-seconds using our model throughput numbers (we'll provide per-model stats).
- Concurrency: for short non-streaming requests we target ~8–16 concurrent requests per GPU depending on model/sequence length. For longer streams concurrency is lower.
- Burst capacity: Dedicated supports a configurable burst buffer (reserved headroom + dynamic burst credits). We can provision a small burst tier for critical SLAs — pricing is add-on per peak minute consumed.
- Queue sizing: if you have short spikes (like your 150 r/s bursts), a small request queue with backlog + SLA-aware drop policies is best — we'll suggest concurrency limits and a queue depth (e.g., 500 requests) in the template based on your numbers.

Please fill the attached sizing template and we'll run a quick calc ahead of the call. Also, what's your desired p99 tail SLA objective for short queries? If you can share p99 we can size the reserved > burst mix accordingly.

Docs: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-redwood-dedicated-sizing
Sizing template attached: Dedicated_Capacity_Sizing_Template.xlsx
